newsitem.title: GERMANY: German publishers see 8 pct growth in 1996 - poll.
newsitem.headline: German publishers see 8 pct growth in 1996 - poll.

text.p: The 50 largest German publishing houses boosted turnover by nearly eight percent last year fuelled by strong growth among the top three companies, trade magazine Horizont said on Wednesday.

Revenues jumped 7.9 percent to 59.5 billion marks during 1996, with the Guetersloh-based media company Bertelsmann leading the industry by a wide margin, Horizont said, summarising the findings of a poll it conducted.
Bertelsmann represents 36.2 percent of the German market's publishing turnover and increased its own turnover by 4.7 percent over 1995 to 21.5 billion marks.

Second-ranked Axel Springer Verlag posted a turnover increase of 6.6 percent to 4.42 billion marks, Horizont said. The third-placed WAZ newspaper group saw growth of 18 percent to 3.3 billion marks in turnover.
